1.title: Network Security Concepts: Models, Addresses, Ports and VPNs
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Network Security Concepts: Models, Addresses, Ports and V P Ns. It covers the exam area four. Networking and Cloud Security Concepts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. The O S I model. The T C P I P model. I P addresses. Ports and common protocols. Virtual private networks. Other network basics. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four. Networking and Cloud Security Concepts (twenty-one point three percent). Exam format: an adaptive exam of one hundred to one hundred twenty-five questions in two hours; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official I S C two C C exam outline.

1.title: The OSI model
1.text: The O S I model. The Open Systems Interconnection (O S I) model describes seven layers of network communication. Data moves down the layers on the sender and up the layers on the receiver.

1.title: The OSI model, continued
1.text: The O S I model. The figure shows this: The seven O S I layers and the four T C P I P layers side by side.

1.title: The OSI model, continued
1.text: The O S I model. seven. Name: Application. Data unit: Data. Examples: H T T P, D N S, S M T P. six. Name: Presentation. Data unit: Data. Examples: Encryption, formats. five. Name: Session. Data unit: Data. Examples: Sessions between hosts. four. Name: Transport. Data unit: Segment (T C P), datagram (U D P). Examples: T C P, U D P, ports. three. Name: Network. Data unit: Packet. Examples: I P addresses, routers. two. Name: Data link. Data unit: Frame. Examples: M A C addresses, switches. one. Name: Physical. Data unit: Bits. Examples: Cables, radio, hubs. Memory aid, top to bottom: "All People Seem To Need Data Processing". Exam tip: Routers work at layer three, switches at layer two, firewalls at layers three to seven. I P address equals layer three; M A C address equals layer two; port equals layer four.

1.title: The TCP/IP model
1.text: The T C P I P model. Application. O S I layers: five to seven. Examples: H T T P, H T T P S, D N S, S M T P. Transport. O S I layers: four. Examples: T C P, U D P. Internet. O S I layers: three. Examples: I P, I C M P. Network access (link). O S I layers: one and two. Examples: Ethernet, Wi-Fi. T C P I P is the model the real internet uses; O S I is the teaching reference. T C P. Connection-oriented and reliable: handshake, acknowledgments, retransmission. U D P. Connectionless and fast: no guarantee; voice, video, D N S queries.

1.title: IP addresses
1.text: I P addresses. I P version four. Size: thirty-two bits, about four point three billion addresses. Example: one hundred ninety-two dot one hundred sixty-eight dot one dot ten. Notes: Four numbers zero to two hundred fifty-five; running out. I P version six. Size: one hundred twenty-eight bits. Example: twenty oh one:db eight::one. Notes: Eight groups of hexadecimal; vast address space; I P sec built in as an option. Private I P version four ranges (not routed on the internet): ten dot zero dot zero dot zero slash eight, one hundred seventy-two dot sixteen dot zero dot zero slash twelve, one hundred ninety-two dot one hundred sixty-eight dot zero dot zero slash sixteen. Network address translation (nat) lets private hosts share one public address.

1.title: Ports and common protocols
1.text: Ports and common protocols. A port (zero to sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-five) names the service on a host. Well-known ports are zero to one thousand twenty-three. twenty, twenty-one. Protocol: F T P. Secure?: No: clear text. twenty-two. Protocol: S S H and S F T P. Secure?: Yes. twenty-three. Protocol: Telnet. Secure?: No. twenty-five. Protocol: S M T P (mail sending). Secure?: Clear text unless protected. fifty-three. Protocol: D N S. Secure?: Not by itself. eighty. Protocol: H T T P. Secure?: No. one ten and one forty-three. Protocol: P O P three or I M A P. Secure?: No; secure versions use nine ninety-five and nine ninety-three. four forty-three. Protocol: H T T P S. Secure?: Yes (T L S). thirty-three eighty-nine. Protocol: Remote Desktop (R D P). Secure?: Needs protection. Exam tip: Replace Telnet with S S H, F T P with S F T P, H T T P with H T T P S. Block or protect any port that is not needed.

1.title: Virtual private networks (VPNs)
1.text: Virtual private networks (V P Ns). A V P N (virtual private network) creates an encrypted tunnel across an untrusted network (the internet). Remote-access V P N. A single user connects to the company network. Site-to-site V P N. Two networks (offices) are joined.

1.title: Virtual private networks (VPNs), continued
1.text: Virtual private networks (V P Ns). I P sec. Works at the network layer; A H (integrity) and E S P (encryption and integrity). T L S (S S L) V P N. Uses T L S; often through a browser or client. A full tunnel sends all traffic through the V P N; a split tunnel sends only company traffic. Exam tip: A V P N protects the data in the tunnel; it does not make the connecting device safe. I P sec works at the network layer; T L S V P Ns work above it.

1.title: Other network basics
1.text: Other network basics. D N S. Turns names into I P addresses. D H C P. Hands out I P settings automatically. A R P. Maps I P address to M A C address on a local network. I C M P. Error and test messages; ping. M A C address. Hardware address of a network card.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. At which O S I layer do routers make forwarding decisions using I P addresses? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Layer three, the network layer. Routers use I P addresses at the network layer, layer three.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A video call prefers speed over perfect delivery. Which transport protocol suits it best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: U D P, which is connectionless and fast. U D P is connectionless and fast, which suits real-time voice and video.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which pair is a clear-text protocol and its secure replacement? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Telnet replaced by S S H for administration. Telnet sends data in clear text and S S H is the encrypted replacement.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. How many bits does an I P version six address have? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: one hundred twenty-eight bits, written in hexadecimal groups. An I P version six address is one hundred twenty-eight bits long, written in hexadecimal groups.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company joins its branch office network to its headquarters network over the internet with encryption. Which solution fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A site-to-site V P N between the networks. A site-to-site V P N joins two networks through an encrypted tunnel.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which address range is private under I P version four? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: one hundred seventy-two dot sixteen dot zero dot zero to one hundred seventy-two dot thirty-one dot two hundred fifty-five dot two hundred fifty-five. one hundred seventy-two dot sixteen dot zero dot zero slash twelve is one of the three private ranges.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many layers does the O S I model have? Answer: Seven. Question two. What is the data unit at layer three? Answer: A packet. Question three. Which port does H T T P S use? Answer: four forty-three.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the port of S S H? Answer: twenty-two. Question five. What does nat do? Answer: Lets private hosts share a public address. Question six. Which V P N sends only company traffic through the tunnel? Answer: A split-tunnel V P N.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. O S I: seven layers; router L three, switch L two, port L four. T C P I P: four layers; T C P reliable, U D P fast. I P: I P version four thirty-two bits, I P version six one hundred twenty-eight bits; private ten, one hundred seventy-two point one six, one hundred ninety-two point one six eight. Ports: twenty-two S S H, twenty-three Telnet, fifty-three D N S, eighty H T T P, four forty-three H T T P S, thirty-three eighty-nine R D P. V P N: encrypted tunnel; remote access or site to site; I P sec, T L S.
